profile.entities: Shree Pushkar Chemicals & Fertilisers Ltd; Madhya Bharat Phosphates Ltd; Kisan Phosphates
profile.subseg: Specialty Textile Dyes; Dye Intermediates (H-Acid, Vinyl Sulphone); SSP Fertilisers; Solar Power
profile.themes: Raw Material Hyper-Inflation; Strategic Production Pause; Capex Delay due to Input Volatility

bull_bear.body: Debt-free core operations; Net Cash position. Rs. 140.68 Cr in non-lien AAA-rated bonds. Preferential allotment (Rs. 30 Cr) to promoters completed. Dividend policy not explicitly detailed but capital preservation for expansion prioritized. No major debt planned for upcoming capex (<30% leverage max).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Sustained raw material inflation (Ammonia/Sulphur) exceeding pass-through ability. Global geopolitical instability affecting energy/feedstock supply. Delay in commissioning Unit 5/6 beyond Q2FY27 leading to further revenue miss. Government subsidy policy changes. Demand suppression in Bangladesh/Global markets due to energy crisis.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic but highly defensive. 'Sit quietly, wait and watch.' Prioritizes long-term survival over short-term volume. Transparent about delaying revenue to protect margins. Views volatility as a 'blessing' for well-capitalized players. Conservative guidance to manage expectations.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management deliberately stopped sales in mid-March Q4 (forgoing ~Rs. 24 Cr revenue) to sell inventory in Q1FY27 at significantly higher prices, creating a hidden Q1 earnings boost. Unit 5 & 6 are physically complete but financially uncapitalized to avoid depreciation/working capital drag during peak input costs. The 'lost' Kharif season is a strategic choice, not a failure of execution.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Growth to be funded through internal accruals and preferential allotment, reflecting strong cash flows and disciplined capital allocation"; the capex slide repeats funding as "Internal accruals & preferential issue".
- FY26 Net Debt/Equity of (0.01)x, i.e. a net-cash position on the deck's own measure.
- "Maintains Rs. 124.91 Cr in non-lien deposits as on 30th June 2026".
- FY26 ROE of 12.2% and ROCE of 15.3%, "reflecting profitability and capital efficiency".
- The deck states no dividend policy or payout figure, and does not size or price the proposed preferential issue.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Chemical Segment: FY26 Rev Rs. 531.8 Cr (+25.2%); Volume 72,423 MT (+27.9%). Q4 Rev Rs. 126.4 Cr; Volume 13,725 MT (+36% YoY). Realization up despite volume surge (H-Acid Rs. 525->750/kg; Vinyl Sulphone Rs. 240->350/kg). Fertiliser Segment: FY26 Rev Rs. 444.8 Cr (+16.5%); Volume 252,777 MT. Q4 Rev Rs. 91.8 Cr; Volume 50,500 MT. Growth driven by improved realization offsetting volume constraints from RM shortage.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "Zero-Waste, Integrated Manufacturing Model": "Interlinked manufacturing setup anchored by the Acid Complex, enabling seamless by-product utilization across divisions" and "Integrated operations optimizing resource and raw material utilization while strengthening cost efficiency across the value chain".
- Six-vertical presence stated on the letterhead — "Speciality Textile Dyes, Dyes Intermediates, Acids, Power, Animal Health & Nutrition, Fertilisers" — with FY26 revenue split as "Fertilisers (46% FY26 Revenue)" and "Chemicals (54% FY26 Revenue)".
- "Comprehensive Manufacturing & Distribution Network": 9 facilities across Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Haryana, "800+ distributors and 14 offices across India", with coverage "across the northern, central, and parts of eastern and southern regions of India".
- Certification-led credentials: "A Government of India Recognised Export House", ISO 9001:2015 & 14001:2015 certified, GOTS approved, ZDHC gateway registered, plus Bluesign and ZDHC certification cited for the dyestuff business.
- Customer sets are named per division: farmers via 800 distributors (fertilisers), cattle & poultry feed manufacturers (animal health & nutrition), manufacturers of synthetic dyes (dye intermediates), and textile dyeing, "particularly for cellulosic fibers (cotton, flax, and wool)" (dyestuff).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Land acquisition] "the Company acquired approximately 30,000 sq. metres of land at Lote Parshuram for Rs. 9.33 Cr, adjacent to its existing Unit 1", to support future expansion at the existing manufacturing location.
- [M&A history] 100% equity acquisition of Kisan Phosphates Pvt Ltd (2018-2019 diversification phase) and 100% equity acquisition of Madhya Bharat Phosphate Pvt Ltd (2021), the latter alongside commencing A.H.N.F production at MBPPL Unit 2 in Madhya Pradesh.
- [Operating environment] Management attributes Q1 FY27 volume declines in both segments to "ongoing global supply chain challenges and elevated raw material prices" and "the prevailing operating environment", with improved realisations offsetting lower volumes.
- [Prior infrastructure] At KPPL the company "Installed sulphuric acid and captive power plants utilizing a waste heat boiler and commissioned a 200 TPD granulation plant" (2016-17), and completed additional capacity of 32,000 MTPA in KPPL (2023).
- [Promoter-led board] Mr. Punit Makharia is Chairman & Managing Director and Mr. Gautam Makharia is Joint Managing Director, alongside three Non-Executive Independent Directors and one Non-Executive Non-Independent Director.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Gross Margin Q4: 38.4%. EBITDA Margin Q4: 10.1%. Cost Pressure: Ammonia Rs. 40->100+/kg; Sulphur Rs. 30->100/kg. Government NBS subsidy increased but capped at 10% hike, insufficient to cover 3x input cost rise. Management expects margin recovery to 8-10% range as finished goods prices re-rate higher in Q1FY27.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: FY27 guidance lowered to Rs. 1,250-1,300 Cr (from Rs. 1,500 Cr) due to lost Kharif season contribution from new units. Margin: Targeting 8-10% EBITDA/PAT mix; conservative 8% PAT visibility. Order Inflow: Deliberately suppressed in March Q4 to capture April-June price hikes. Capex/Commissioning: Unit 5 & 6 (90-95% complete) held back; trial production possible within 1 month but commercially paused until raw material (Ammonia/Sulphur) pricing stabilizes; likely commissioning Q1/Q2 FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: No formal order book; spot market driven. Management intentionally withheld ~Rs. 24 Cr sales in late March Q4 to realize higher realizations in Q1FY27.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Unit 5 (Dyes) and Unit 6 (Fertiliser expansion) ready for trial but commercially paused to avoid working capital strain at peak input costs. Meghnagar expansion (Rs. 350 Cr capex) in planning; funding via internal accruals (Rs. 170 Cr available) + potential minor debt (25-30%). Solar capacity expanding to 20.6 MW DC (1.1 MW commissioned in Haryana; 10 MW Nanded in progress).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Shree Pushkar delivered steady FY26 growth (21% revenue) but strategically halted dispatches and delayed Unit 5/6 commissioning in Q4 due to tripled raw material costs (Ammonia/Sulphur) outpacing subsidy adjustments. Management prioritizes margin protection over volume, expecting a 'blessing' of inventory gains in Q1FY27 while deferring new capacity contribution until market pricing stabilizes.
